(A) sm-3:3342-3345 "Use standard contact space (ℝ³, ker(dz−y dx)), with positive transverse orientation z′−yx′>0 (Etnyre … for the conventions)". Convention + provenance, no field (FR-SC-8). Correct: every contact form of the accepted layer is literally v_z − p_y v_x (`SM.contactForm` TransverseFront.lean:118; `SM.lcContactForm` LinkingCalculus.lean:553; `SM.GenericFront.alpha` GenericFront.lean:52; `SM.TransverseNeighborhood.alpha` TransverseNeighborhood.lean:47 — all printed by the snippet as `w 2 − p 1 * w 0`), and `IsPositiveTransverse T = ∀θ, 0 < alpha (T θ) (deriv T θ)` (GenericFront.lean:62), `TransverseKnot.positive` (TransverseFront.lean:581) is z′ − y x′ > 0. The bridging theorems S:78-92 (`lcContactForm_toE3`, `alpha_eq_lcContactForm`, `gf_alpha_eq_lcContactForm`, `isPositiveTransverse_iff`) are proved in the built library with standard axioms only. Precedent ng:finite-word applies.

(B) sm-3:3345-3351 "for an oriented Legendrian front with downward and upward cusp counts D, U". Rendered as the binder `IsLegendrianFrontOf L F` (S:162-165): `GenericFrontHyp L` = `IsEmbeddedCircle L ∧ IsLegendrian L` (GenericFront.lean:178-183, 55-65: smooth 2π-periodic injective immersed circle with α(L′)=0; orientation = parameter direction), `F.c = 1`, and `(F.comp i).γ t = GenericFront.front L (2πt)` = (x(2πt), z(2πt)) (GenericFront.lean:123). So F is the xz-front of the oriented Legendrian knot L, traversed in L's orientation, on the accepted class `SmoothFront` of ng:front-domain (FrontSmooth.lean:305-340). D = `F.downCount`, U = `F.upCount` (FrontSmooth.lean:724-726): `IsDownCusp p := IsCusp p ∧ cuspDisc p < 0`, `cuspDisc = x″·det(γ″,γ‴)` (FrontSmooth.lean:446-457). I re-derived the sign: the arm after the cusp lies on the side of the tangent line ℝγ″ where det(γ″,·) has the sign of det(γ″,γ‴); that side is the upper one iff x″>0; hence upper-arm→lower-arm ⇔ x″·det(γ″,γ‴)<0. This is the document's own "A downward cusp is traversed from its locally upper arm to its locally lower arm" (ng:front-domain, sm-3:1825-1841, accepted row 73) and is Etnyre's down cusp (the orientation passes downward through the cusp); fd:contact's proof (sm-3:3452-3457) confirms the same count D gives sl_Ng = w − D. Class narrowing: knots only (c = 1) and fronts of the ng:front-domain class (semicubical cusps with x″≠0 — for a Legendrian front det(γ″,γ‴)=2y′x″² so this is exactly x″≠0 ∧ y′≠0, the exact-germ genericity of row 87 — transverse double points, no triple point, cusps alone; `no_vertical` is automatic since z′=yx′). A WEAKENING only (FR-SC-2); the consumer's L_T is inside.

(C) sm-3:3349-3351 "every cusp of an oriented front is traversed either downward or upward, so the total cusp count in his tb formula is D+U". Justificatory remark; no field. Correct: it is the accepted `SmoothFront.downCount_add_upCount : D + U = cuspSet.card` (FrontSmooth.lean:740), and the tb field uses the printed (D+U)/2 literally (FR-SC-6).

(D) sm-3:3352 `r=(D−U)/2` → field `rotation` (S:196-197): `r L = ((F.downCount:ℝ) − F.upCount)/2` under the binder. Word-for-word. `tb=w−(D+U)/2` → field `thurston_bennequin` (S:200-201): `tb L = (F.writhe:ℝ) − ((F.downCount:ℝ) + F.upCount)/2`. Word-for-word; w = `F.writhe = Σ_{q∈crossingPairs} crossSign q.1 q.2` with `crossingPairs` = each double point once in over-first order, over = smaller slope dz/dx (FrontSmooth.lean:681-682, 526, 728), `crossSign = sgn det(u_O,u_U)`, `det u v = u.1·v.2 − u.2·v.1` (printed by snippet) — the standard sign (sm-3:1908-1912 check `det (1,−1) (1,1) = 2`, FrontSmooth.lean:360-362). Smaller-slope-over is Etnyre's front rule (y = dz/dx, observer at −y; fd:contact 3432-3436 "For a Legendrian front this is also the smaller-slope rule"), and (x,z) is a positive basis for the observer at ν=−∂_y (det(∂x,∂z,−∂y)=1, 3436-3443), so w is the front writhe of the literature.

(E) sm-3:3353 `sl(T₊(L)) = tb(L) − r(L)` → field `pushoff_self_linking` (S:204-205): for L with front F and EVERY T′ with `GenericFront.IsPositivePushoff L T′`, `slCircle T′ = tb L − r L`. `IsPositivePushoff L T′ = ∃ ε b B, IsPushoffAnnulus L ε b B ∧ ∃ s₀, 0<s₀<b ∧ T′ = B(·,s₀)` (GenericFront.lean:88-90); the annulus is smooth, 2π-periodic, embedded, immersed, with core L, tangent plane nowhere inside ξ (so along the Legendrian core α(∂_sB)≠0 and L is a leaf of its characteristic foliation), and positive transverse circles for 0<s<b (GenericFront.lean:74-86; byte-identical to row 84's TransverseNeighborhood.lean:120-136, FR-TN-4). This is the document's own accepted meaning of "positive pushoff" (sm-3:2497-2502 "A sufficiently small positive circle is therefore the positive pushoff in the source convention"). Truth on the accepted definitions: all positive circles of one annulus are joined by a transverse isotopy (row 88 `self_linking_invariant` keeps sl constant, LinkingCalculusRow.lean:68-71); a small circle B(·,s₁) is C¹-close to L along a normal transverse to ξ, hence a graph in L's standard J¹(S¹)-neighbourhood, where every positive transverse graph is transversely isotopic to {y=−ε,z=0} by the linear interpolation (1−t)(z′−y)+tε>0 — so every Lean-sense pushoff lies in the single class T₊(L) that the printed notation presupposes; the sign of α(∂_sB) at the core is immaterial (the document's own model has arbitrary κ≠0, sm-3:2485-2502). Positive = α(T′)>0 matches "positive transverse orientation z′−yx′>0", so the formula asserted is Etnyre's (17) for T₊ and not the T₋ variant (w−U); fd:contact 3452-3459 fixes this reading ("identifies Ng's pushoff as Etnyre's positive pushoff"). `sl`: `slCircle T = selfLinking 2π T ε₀` with ε₀ = `Classical.choose (fd_linking_calculus.transverse_uniform 2π (fun _ => T) …)` when `IsPositiveTransverseEmbedding 2π T`, else 0 (S:141-145); `selfLinking P T ε = linking P T (pushoff T (fun _ => ey) ε)`, `ey = ∂_y`, `linking` = the normalised Gauss integral (1/4π)∫∫ G·(G_u×G_v) (LinkingCalculus.lean:361-380, 549-574) — the document's fd:framed-linking number (sm-3:2820-2824), radius-free by row 88's `self_linking_invariant` (ε=ε₀ is admissible since the clause is ε≤ε₀), real-valued (FR-SC-4, FR-SC-10); identification with the literature's sl is the document's rem:sl-convention (3012-3022), cited by fd:contact's proof (3441-3443). The 0-default is never exercised: a pushoff circle is smooth, 2π-periodic (`periodic`), embedded (`injective`, `IsPushoffAnnulus.circle` GenericFront.lean:5371) and positive (`positive`), and `GenericFront.alpha = lcContactForm` definitionally (FR-SC-9).

(F) sm-3:3355-3357 provenance parenthesis (Geiges Prop 3.5.9; Etnyre (7) → Remark 2.14 without proof): commentary, no field. Correct.

(G) sm-3:3358-3363 "For a generic positive transverse front (Definition def:transverse-front), self-linking equals its front writhe: [citations]" → field `transverse_front_writhe` (S:209): `∀ K : TransverseKnot, sl K = (K.front.writhe : ℝ)`. `TransverseKnot` (TransverseFront.lean:571-595) is exactly def:transverse-front's knot (sm-3:3328-3339; the brief's pointer 341-343 is off — the definition is at 3328-3339); `K.front` is its xz diagram with over = smaller y (TransverseFront.lean:734-744), `writhe = Σ_{crossingPairs} sgn det_xz(u_O,u_U)` (TransverseFront.lean:278, 389) = the RHS of fd:front-writhe; `sl K = slCircle K.circle`, `K.circle θ = toE3 (K.T (θ/2π))` (S:101, 150), a 2π-periodic positive transverse embedding (positivity scales by 1/2π), so again the on-class branch. "The knot T is named separately" (3339-3340) is honoured: the statement is over K, and every generic front is K.front for some K (`IsGenericPositiveTransverseFront`, TransverseFront.lean:795). Citations: commentary.

(H) sm-3:3363-3364 "These are the local front and pushoff source formulas only": scope; no field; the structure has exactly the four printed formulas and nothing else. sm-3:3365 \status: metadata.

(I) ∃-form (S:221 `axiom src_contact : ∃ r tb : (ℝ → E3) → ℝ, SrcContactClauses r tb`; FR-SC-1). The document never defines r or tb, so no Lean term can name the literature's invariants; the printed display's document-expressible content is the substituted consequence, and the built `src_contact_iff_consequence` (S:254-256) proves the ∃-form ↔ (sl(T₊)=w−D on the Legendrian class ∧ sl=w on the transverse class) with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only. Consistency of the ∃ across fronts is guaranteed by `IsLegendrianFrontOf.unique` (S:168-170, proved). Neither stronger nor weaker in the document's language; pattern of the accepted `lit_homfly`, `lp_lm`. `rot`/`tb` (S:224-226) are Classical.choose witnesses and are claimed to be nothing more.

Nothing in the axiom is stronger than printed: every field is guarded by the printed class (front of an oriented Legendrian knot; positive pushoff in the document's sense; generic positive transverse front), and all sign conventions (over = smaller y ↔ observer at −∂_y, det_xz, ∂_y pushoff, positive = α>0) agree with fd:linking-calculus, def:transverse-front and fd:contact's printed proof. Docstring quotations (S:211-217, 195, 198, 202, 206) match the registry with citation parentheticals elided. Verdict: faithful.
discrepancies: Reading, not defect (FR-SC-3): the printed `T₊(L)` is a transverse-isotopy class; the field quantifies over EVERY circle B(·,s₀), 0<s₀<b, of EVERY `GenericFront.IsPushoffAnnulus` (no requirement that circles with s<0 be negative transverse, no smallness of s₀). Equivalent to the printed statement given the literature's well-definedness of T₊(L) (all such circles lie in one class: within an annulus by the s-family, across annuli via C¹-closeness to L and the standard Legendrian neighbourhood); the document itself adopts this notion at sm-3:2497-2502 and row 84/87.

Reading, not defect (FR-SC-1): the ∃-form does not identify `rot`/`tb` with the literature's rotation number and Thurston–Bennequin invariant; the document defines neither, and the built `src_contact_iff_consequence` shows the axiom's content is exactly sl(T₊)=w−D on the Legendrian class and sl=w on the transverse class.
Neutral: r, tb, sl are ℝ-valued (S:194, 141) where the literature's are (half-)integers; equalities compare reals with ℕ/ℤ casts, as fd:contact does (FR-SC-10).

Docstring only: S:160 attributes "the positive y axis goes into the page" to Etnyre §2.2 (3); not checkable from the permitted files, but it agrees with fd:contact's printed proof (sm-3:3432-3436, observer at −∂_y).
Brief pointer: def:transverse-front is at sm-3:3328-3339, not 341-343 (341-343 is the general diagram sentence of def:gauss-record's context); no effect on the declaration.
weaker_than_source: Legendrian formulas (rotation, thurston_bennequin, pushoff_self_linking) hold only for KNOTS: `IsLegendrianFrontOf` forces `F.c = 1`; Etnyre's fronts may be links (FR-SC-2).

Legendrian formulas hold only for L whose xz-projection lies on ng:front-domain's class `SmoothFront` (finitely many semicubical cusps with x″≠0 and, for a Legendrian front, y′≠0 at each cusp; finitely many transverse double points; no triple point; cusps on no other branch). Legendrian knots with non-generic fronts receive no formula (the third formula, Etnyre's Lemma 2.22, holds for every Legendrian knot in the literature).

The ∃-form asserts nothing about r, tb beyond the two defining formulas on the front class (values off the class are unconstrained; no identification with the contact-framing linking number or the winding of L′ in ξ).
Integrality of sl is not asserted (it follows from field 4 for transverse knots and from field 3 via w−D for pushoffs).

U = upCount (cuspDisc > 0); D+U = #cusps is the accepted downCount_add_upCount (FrontSmooth 740) — no field, correct (FR-SC-6). w = F.writhe = Σ over crossingPairs (each double point once, ordered over-first with over = smaller slope = smaller y = dz/dx for a Legendrian front, FrontSmooth 516-529, 681-682, 728) of crossSign = if 0 < det(vel_O, vel_U) then 1 else −1, det u v = u.1·v.2 − u.2·v.1 (Polygon.lean 16) = det_xz(u_O,u_U) of fd:contact 3437; the (2π)² velocity scaling from the reparametrisation does not change signs. The over rule and sign are those fixed by fd:contact's printed proof (3429-3439: observer at −∂_y, smaller y over, (x̂,ẑ,−ŷ) positive) and by the accepted standard-crossing check (FrontSmooth 343-362). (3) excerpt 17 `r = (D−U)/2`: field rotation (statement 196-197) `r L = (↑D − ↑U)/2` — exact. `tb = w − (D+U)/2`: field thurston_bennequin (200-201) `tb L = ↑w − (↑D + ↑U)/2` — exact, with D+U written as printed. (4) excerpt 18 `sl(T₊(L)) = tb(L) − r(L)`: field pushoff_self_linking (204-205) `∀ T', GenericFront.IsPositivePushoff L T' → slCircle T' = tb L − r L`. Every such circle is in slCircle's class: IsPushoffAnnulus.circle (GenericFront 5371) gives IsEmbeddedCircle, .positive gives IsPositiveTransverse, and IsPositiveTransverseEmbedding (2π) T' (LinkingCalculus 559-562: IsSmoothCircle + injective mod k·2π + 0 < lcContactForm) is exactly those fields — so the 0-default of slCircle is never exercised here (FR-SC-9). Truth on the accepted definitions (independent derivation, not relying on the disclosed numeric probe): the annulus is transverse to ξ along L (IsPushoffAnnulus.transverse at s=0 with α(L′)=0 forces α(∂_sB)≠0), so its framing of L is the contact framing and lk(L, T') = tb(L); the characteristic line field ℓ = TA ∩ ξ is smooth on the annulus, gives the annulus framing of T' inside ξ|_{T'}, and its winding relative to the global section ∂_y is constant in s and equals at s=0 the winding of L′ = x′E₁ + y′∂_y in the dα-positive frame (E₁,∂_y), i.e. the Lagrangian rotation number, which equals (D−U)/2 with the Lean's down cusps (a down cusp is a counterclockwise crossing of the y′-axis); positive transversality makes N(T') ≅ ξ|_{T'} orientation-preserving (α∧dα = dx∧dy∧dz), and a +1 framing twist raises lk by +1 (checked on the unknot), giving sl(T') = tb(L) − r(L) = w − D for every positive circle of every pushoff annulus. So the field asserts nothing outside the printed class and is true. (5) excerpt 23-27 "For a generic positive transverse front (Definition def:transverse-front), self-linking equals its front writhe": field transverse_front_writhe (209) `∀ K : TransverseKnot, sl K = ↑K.front.writhe`. The identification with the literature's sl is the document's own rem:sl-convention (3012-3022), cited by fd:contact's proof 3440-3442 — correctly not a field. r and tb are typed (ℝ → E3) → ℝ (real-valued, per parametrised curve) and are characterised only through the two front formulas on the class; their literature meaning (rotation of the tangent in ξ, linking with the contact framing) is not transcribed because the document never defines them. The ∃-form therefore says nothing about the literature's actual r, tb beyond the printed display (FR-SC-1, FR-SC-10).
sl is real-valued (fd:framed-linking); integrality of sl on transverse knots is a consequence of the transverse clause, not asserted separately (FR-SC-10).
